result.title: When frequency domain classification is superior to spatial
result.summary: Modern image classification models largely rely on local characteristics and feature extraction for their predictions. This focused approach works well in the spatial domain, but reportedly falls short in the frequency domain, even though both representations contain the same information. This study demonstrates that the significant reduction in accuracy in the frequency domain stems from the lack of local features. Locally swapping data in the frequency domain significantly decreases its inverse spatial domain accuracy, even below that of the frequency domain; however, the frequency domain accuracy remains relatively constant. Moreover, the use of datasets containing global features in the spatial domain yields higher accuracy in the frequency domain. Using these results, a hybrid model is constructed, combining one model trained only in the frequency domain and another trained only in the spatial domain to achieve higher classification accuracy. The proposed visual geometry group (VGG) and vision transformer (ViT) architectures are trained on the ImageNet-100, WikiArt, DTD, FMD, PSVRT, and KTH-TIPS2-b datasets and evaluated.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察频域图像分类精度低于空域的原因，在频域内局部交换数据以验证局部特征缺失的影响力，并将仅用频域训练与仅用空域训练的模型组合成混合模型以提升分类精度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对局部特征缺失导致表示失效、以及频域与空域互补融合的分析，可能为 LVR 中视觉细节是否保留在内部状态、多表示组合筛选提供类比线索，但论文不涉及推理过程或 latent 状态，需较多核查。
